$comment: Cold tier, and the widest blast radius in the whole configuration: an enabled server is a tool every agent can reach. Nothing is enabled by default. To enable one, move it from `disabled` into `servers` and fill in owner, trust, scope and version. harness doctor refuses an enabled server that is missing any of those, or that carries a literal credential.

filesystem.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
filesystem.trust: reads and writes any file under the workspace folder
filesystem.scope: workspace only; a wider root gives every agent read access to the machine
filesystem.version: pin an exact version before enabling

github.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
github.trust: reads issues, pull requests and code for every repository the token can see
github.scope: use a fine-grained token limited to the repositories that need it, read-only unless a workflow genuinely writes
github.version: pin an exact version before enabling

aws.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
aws.trust: acts as the named AWS profile; whatever that role can do, an agent can do
aws.scope: use a read-only role for review work; a role that can apply infrastructure needs the Q4 quadrant and a human at the keyboard
aws.version: pin an exact version before enabling

azure-devops.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
azure-devops.trust: reads work items, repositories, pull requests, pipelines and wiki for every project the signed-in identity can see
azure-devops.scope: reading only. Writes go through core/tools/ado/*.mjs, which build the command, support --dry-run and redact secrets. Enabling a write path here would move those actions back into the model territory
azure-devops.version: pin an exact version before enabling
